views.name: cdc_wonder_cause_of_death_1999_2024
views.comment: National deaths by year and ICD-10 sub-chapter, 1999-2024 — cdc_wonder_cause_of_death (D76, 1999-2020) unioned with cdc_wonder_cause_of_death_2018_2024 (D158, 2018-2024), preferring D158 for the 2018-2020 years both cover so the combined series never double-counts.
views.sql: SELECT year, icd_subchapter, icd_subchapter_code, deaths, population, crude_rate FROM cdc_wonder_cause_of_death WHERE CAST(year AS INTEGER) < 2018 UNION ALL SELECT year, icd_subchapter, icd_subchapter_code, deaths, population, crude_rate FROM cdc_wonder_cause_of_death_2018_2024

views.name: cdc_wonder_multiple_cause_of_death_1999_2024
views.comment: National deaths by year and MCD Drug/Alcohol Induced Cause category, 1999-2024 — cdc_wonder_multiple_cause_of_death (D77, 1999-2020) unioned with cdc_wonder_multiple_cause_of_death_2018_2024 (D157, 2018-2024), preferring D157 for the 2018-2020 years both cover so the combined series never double-counts. This is the multiple-cause series (a cause counts if listed anywhere among a death's up to 20 causes) — the standard basis for drug overdose mortality trend analysis.
views.sql: SELECT year, cause, deaths, population, crude_rate FROM cdc_wonder_multiple_cause_of_death WHERE CAST(year AS INTEGER) < 2018 UNION ALL SELECT year, cause, deaths, population, crude_rate FROM cdc_wonder_multiple_cause_of_death_2018_2024

views.name: who_health_snapshot
views.comment: Headline WHO GHO indicators pivoted wide: one row per country x year with life expectancy, healthy life expectancy, under-5 mortality, and UHC service coverage (country rows, both-sexes). International complement to the U.S. openFDA tables; join to ref.countries for names/regions.
views.sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  MAX(CASE WHEN indicator_code = 'WHOSIS_000001' THEN value_numeric END) AS life_expectancy,
  MAX(CASE WHEN indicator_code = 'WHOSIS_000002' THEN value_numeric END) AS healthy_life_expectancy,
  MAX(CASE WHEN indicator_code = 'MDG_0000000001' THEN value_numeric END) AS under5_mortality_rate,
  MAX(CASE WHEN indicator_code = 'UHC_INDEX_REPORTED' THEN value_numeric END) AS uhc_service_index
FROM who_gho_indicators WHERE is_aggregate = FALSE
  AND (sex = 'BTSX' OR sex IS NULL)
GROUP BY country_code, year

views.name: drug_profile
views.comment: Complete drug profile: NDC product joined to FDA approval record and RxNorm concept. Left joins preserve NDC products that lack an approval record or rxcui mapping.
views.sql:
SELECT
  n.product_ndc,
  n.generic_name,
  n.brand_name,
  n.labeler_name,
  n.dosage_form,
  n.route,
  n.product_type,
  n.application_number,
  n.rxcui,
  r.name      AS rxnorm_name,
  r.tty       AS rxnorm_tty,
  a.sponsor_name,
  a.marketing_status,
  a.latest_submission_date
FROM fda_ndc_products n LEFT JOIN fda_drug_approvals a ON n.application_number = a.application_number LEFT JOIN rxnorm_drugs r       ON n.rxcui = r.rxcui

views.name: trial_full
views.comment: Denormalised clinical trial view: one row per trial with conditions and interventions aggregated into semicolon-delimited strings.
views.sql:
SELECT
  t.nct_id,
  t.brief_title,
  t.overall_status,
  t.study_type,
  t.phase,
  t.enrollment_count,
  t.lead_sponsor,
  t.funder_type,
  t.start_date,
  t.primary_completion_date,
  t.completion_date,
  t.first_submit_date,
  t.last_update_date,
  t.brief_summary,
  t.has_results,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT c.condition_name,  '; ') AS conditions,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT i.intervention_name, '; ') AS interventions
FROM clinical_trials t LEFT JOIN clinical_trial_conditions   c ON t.nct_id = c.nct_id LEFT JOIN clinical_trial_interventions i ON t.nct_id = i.nct_id GROUP BY
  t.nct_id, t.brief_title, t.overall_status, t.study_type, t.phase,
  t.enrollment_count, t.lead_sponsor, t.funder_type, t.start_date,
  t.primary_completion_date, t.completion_date, t.first_submit_date,
  t.last_update_date, t.brief_summary, t.has_results

views.name: medicaid_drug_spend
views.comment: Medicaid drug utilization enriched with NDC product details and RxNorm name, at the same (state, year, quarter, ndc, utilization_type) grain as medicaid_drug_utilization — no aggregation. Enables spend analysis by brand, generic, labeler, and rxcui. For annual state+drug totals see drug_spend_trends; for state+year totals across all drugs see medicaid_spend_by_state_geo.
views.sql:
SELECT
  m.state,
  m.year,
  m.quarter,
  m.ndc,
  m.utilization_type,
  m.product_name             AS medicaid_product_name,
  n.brand_name,
  n.generic_name,
  n.labeler_name,
  n.dosage_form,
  r.name                     AS rxnorm_name,
  r.tty                      AS rxnorm_tty,
  m.units_reimbursed,
  m.number_of_prescriptions,
  m.total_amount_reimbursed,
  m.medicaid_amount_reimbursed,
  m.non_medicaid_amount_reimbursed,
  m.suppression_used
FROM medicaid_drug_utilization m LEFT JOIN fda_ndc_products n ON m.product_ndc9 = n.product_ndc9 LEFT JOIN rxnorm_drugs r     ON n.rxcui = r.rxcui

views.name: public_health_indicators
views.comment: State-year summary combining CDC mortality totals (total_deaths, avg_age_adjusted_rate, distinct_causes) with BRFSS risk-factor averages (brfss_question_count, avg_risk_factor_pct) via FULL OUTER JOIN — rows where BRFSS has data but mortality does not appear with NULL death columns and vice versa. For a mortality-driven version with state geography see health_social_equity; for unaggregated per-cause/per-question detail see mortality_brfss_by_state.
views.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(m.year,  b.year)  AS year,
  COALESCE(m.state, b.state) AS state,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.deaths AS BIGINT))       AS total_deaths,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(m.age_adjusted_rate AS DOUBLE)) AS avg_age_adjusted_rate,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.cause_name)             AS distinct_causes,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.question)               AS brfss_question_count,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(b.pct AS DOUBLE))           AS avg_risk_factor_pct
FROM cdc_mortality m FULL OUTER JOIN cdc_brfss b
  ON m.state = b.state AND m.year = b.year
WHERE (m.source_type = 'annual' OR m.source_type IS NULL) GROUP BY COALESCE(m.year, b.year), COALESCE(m.state, b.state)

views.name: hospital_quality_by_state
views.comment: State-level hospital quality summary: counts, average ratings, and quality tier breakdown, aggregated from all cms_hospital_quality facility rows in the state. For facility-level detail with county geography see hospital_with_geography; for a county-level aggregate see hospital_county_summary.
views.sql:
SELECT
  state,
  COUNT(*)                                                       AS hospital_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN overall_rating NOT IN ('Not Available', '')
             THEN 1 END)                                         AS rated_count,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(overall_rating AS DOUBLE))                        AS avg_overall_rating,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN TRY_CAST(overall_rating AS INTEGER) >= 4
             THEN 1 END)                                         AS high_quality_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN hospital_type = 'Acute Care Hospitals'
             THEN 1 END)                                         AS acute_care_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN emergency_services = 'Yes' THEN 1 END)         AS with_emergency_services,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN birthing_friendly = 'Yes'  THEN 1 END)         AS birthing_friendly_count
FROM cms_hospital_quality GROUP BY state

views.name: hospital_with_geography
views.comment: Hospital quality records enriched with county FIPS, county name, and rural-urban classification via the dominant-county ZIP crosswalk. One row per facility (same grain as cms_hospital_quality) — see hospital_quality_by_state for a state-level aggregate and hospital_county_summary for a county-level aggregate.
views.sql:
SELECT
  h.facility_id,
  h.facility_name,
  h.address,
  h.city,
  h.state,
  h.zip_code,
  h.county,
  h.hospital_type,
  h.hospital_ownership,
  h.emergency_services,
  h.overall_rating,
  h.mort_measures_better,
  h.mort_measures_worse,
  h.safety_measures_better,
  h.safety_measures_worse,
  h.readm_measures_better,
  h.readm_measures_worse,
  h.patient_exp_rating,
  h.birthing_friendly,
  xw.county_fips,
  c.county_name  AS geo_county_name,
  ruc.rucc_code,
  ruc.rucc_description,
  ruc.metro_nonmetro
FROM cms_hospital_quality h LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT zip, county_fips,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zip ORDER BY res_ratio DESC) AS rn
  FROM "geo"."zip_county_crosswalk"
) xw ON h.zip_code = xw.zip AND xw.rn = 1 LEFT JOIN "geo"."counties"               c   ON xw.county_fips = c.county_fips LEFT JOIN "geo"."rural_urban_continuum"  ruc ON xw.county_fips = ruc.county_fips

views.name: medicaid_spend_by_state_geo
views.comment: Medicaid spend aggregated by state and year across all drugs, enriched with state name and FIPS for choropleth-ready geographic analysis. For a per-drug breakout see drug_spend_trends, and for unaggregated per-quarter rows see medicaid_drug_spend.
views.sql:
SELECT
  s.state_fips,
  s.state_name,
  m.state,
  m.year,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.total_amount_reimbursed    AS DOUBLE)) AS total_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.medicaid_amount_reimbursed AS DOUBLE)) AS medicaid_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.number_of_prescriptions    AS BIGINT)) AS total_prescriptions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.ndc)                                  AS distinct_drugs
FROM medicaid_drug_utilization m LEFT JOIN "geo"."states" s ON m.state = s.state_abbr GROUP BY s.state_fips, s.state_name, m.state, m.year

views.name: mortality_brfss_by_state
views.comment: CDC annual mortality joined to BRFSS risk factors, both enriched with state geography. One row per state/year/cause/question combination (LEFT JOIN, so every mortality cause row is paired with every matching BRFSS question row) — filter on cause_name and question to avoid cross-product explosion. For pre-aggregated state/year totals see public_health_indicators (full outer join, retains BRFSS-only rows) or health_social_equity (mortality-driven, with geography).
views.sql:
SELECT
  gs.state_fips,
  gs.state_name,
  m.state,
  m.year,
  m.cause_name,
  m.full_cause_name,
  m.deaths,
  m.age_adjusted_rate,
  b.question,
  b.category,
  b.topic,
  b.response,
  b.pct          AS risk_factor_pct,
  b.sample_size,
  b.break_out,
  b.break_out_category
FROM cdc_mortality m LEFT JOIN cdc_brfss b
  ON m.state = b.state AND m.year = b.year
LEFT JOIN "geo"."states" gs ON m.state = gs.state_abbr WHERE m.source_type = 'annual'

views.name: drug_manufacturer_span
views.comment: Connects drug manufacturers across FDA approval, NDC catalog, and Medicaid spend. One row per labeler+application. Enables manufacturer market-size and reach analysis.
views.sql:
SELECT
  n.labeler_name,
  n.application_number,
  a.sponsor_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT n.product_ndc)                              AS distinct_products,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.state)                                    AS states_dispensed,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.total_amount_reimbursed AS DOUBLE))         AS total_medicaid_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.number_of_prescriptions AS BIGINT))         AS total_prescriptions
FROM fda_ndc_products n LEFT JOIN fda_drug_approvals        a ON n.application_number = a.application_number LEFT JOIN medicaid_drug_utilization m ON n.product_ndc9 = m.product_ndc9 GROUP BY n.labeler_name, n.application_number, a.sponsor_name

views.name: rxnorm_medicaid_bridge
views.comment: Connects RxNorm clinical concepts to Medicaid spending via NDC codes. One row per rxcui — enables clinical terminology to spending analysis.
views.sql:
SELECT
  r.rxcui,
  r.name                                                     AS rxnorm_name,
  r.tty                                                      AS rxnorm_tty,
  COUNT(DISTINCT n.product_ndc)                              AS distinct_ndcs,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.state)                                    AS states_with_spending,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.total_amount_reimbursed AS DOUBLE))         AS total_medicaid_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.number_of_prescriptions AS BIGINT))         AS total_prescriptions
FROM rxnorm_drugs r LEFT JOIN fda_ndc_products          n ON r.rxcui = n.rxcui LEFT JOIN medicaid_drug_utilization m ON n.product_ndc9 = m.product_ndc9 GROUP BY r.rxcui, r.name, r.tty

views.name: hospital_county_summary
views.comment: Aggregates CMS hospital quality metrics to county level via ZIP-county crosswalk. One row per county — enables county-level healthcare access and quality analysis. See hospital_with_geography for the underlying facility-level rows with county geography, and hospital_quality_by_state for a state-level aggregate.
views.sql:
SELECT
  c.county_fips,
  c.county_name,
  c.state_fips,
  gs.state_abbr,
  COUNT(h.facility_id)                                                       AS facility_count,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(h.overall_rating AS DOUBLE))                                  AS avg_rating,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN TRY_CAST(h.overall_rating AS INTEGER) >= 4 THEN 1 END)     AS high_quality_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN h.emergency_services = 'Yes' THEN 1 END)                   AS with_emergency,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(h.mort_measures_better AS DOUBLE))                            AS avg_mortality_better,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(h.readm_measures_better AS DOUBLE))                           AS avg_readmission_better
FROM cms_hospital_quality h LEFT JOIN "geo"."zip_county_crosswalk" zc ON h.zip_code = zc.zip LEFT JOIN "geo"."counties"              c  ON zc.county_fips = c.county_fips LEFT JOIN "geo"."states"               gs  ON c.state_fips = gs.state_fips GROUP BY c.county_fips, c.county_name, c.state_fips, gs.state_abbr

views.name: drug_spend_trends
views.comment: Annual Medicaid drug spend aggregated from quarterly utilization data, enriched with NDC product details. One row per state+year+ndc — enables year-over-year spend trend analysis by brand, generic, and labeler. For unaggregated per-quarter rows see medicaid_drug_spend; for state+year totals across all drugs see medicaid_spend_by_state_geo.
views.sql:
SELECT
  m.state,
  m.year,
  m.ndc,
  n.brand_name,
  n.generic_name,
  n.labeler_name,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.total_amount_reimbursed    AS DOUBLE)) AS annual_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.medicaid_amount_reimbursed AS DOUBLE)) AS medicaid_spend,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.number_of_prescriptions    AS BIGINT)) AS annual_prescriptions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.quarter)                              AS quarters_reported
FROM medicaid_drug_utilization m LEFT JOIN fda_ndc_products n ON m.product_ndc9 = n.product_ndc9 GROUP BY m.state, m.year, m.ndc, n.brand_name, n.generic_name, n.labeler_name

views.name: health_social_equity
views.comment: State-year health equity view: CDC annual mortality (deaths summed across all causes — cause_name is not broken out in this view) layered with BRFSS behavioral risk-factor prevalence, enriched with state name/FIPS geography. One row per state+year (LEFT JOIN from mortality, so BRFSS-only state-years are dropped). For a per-cause, per-question breakdown see mortality_brfss_by_state; for a version that also retains BRFSS-only rows see public_health_indicators.
views.sql:
SELECT
  m.state                                          AS state_abbr,
  m.year,
  gs.state_name,
  gs.state_fips,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.deaths AS BIGINT))                AS total_deaths,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(m.age_adjusted_rate AS DOUBLE))     AS avg_mortality_rate,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.question)                       AS brfss_questions_tracked,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(b.pct AS DOUBLE))                   AS avg_risk_factor_pct
FROM cdc_mortality m LEFT JOIN "geo"."states" gs ON m.state = gs.state_abbr LEFT JOIN cdc_brfss b       ON m.state = b.state AND m.year = b.year WHERE m.source_type = 'annual' GROUP BY m.state, m.year, gs.state_name, gs.state_fips

views.name: weather_health_correlation
views.comment: Links annual CDC mortality to NOAA CDO monthly climate summaries by state and year. Temperature and precipitation are pivoted from long to wide via conditional aggregation. One row per state+year — enables climate-health correlation analysis.
views.sql:
SELECT
  m.state                                                                          AS state_abbr,
  m.year,
  gs.state_name,
  gs.state_fips,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(m.deaths AS BIGINT))                                                AS total_deaths,
  AVG(TRY_CAST(m.age_adjusted_rate AS DOUBLE))                                     AS avg_mortality_rate,
  AVG(CASE WHEN w.datatype = 'TAVG' THEN TRY_CAST(w.value AS DOUBLE) END)          AS avg_temp_c,
  MIN(CASE WHEN w.datatype = 'TMIN' THEN TRY_CAST(w.value AS DOUBLE) END)          AS min_monthly_temp_c,
  MAX(CASE WHEN w.datatype = 'TMAX' THEN TRY_CAST(w.value AS DOUBLE) END)          AS max_monthly_temp_c,
  SUM(CASE WHEN w.datatype = 'PRCP' THEN TRY_CAST(w.value AS DOUBLE) END)          AS total_precip_mm
FROM cdc_mortality m LEFT JOIN "geo"."states" gs ON m.state = gs.state_abbr LEFT JOIN "weather"."cdo_monthly_summaries" w
  ON gs.state_fips = w.state_fips AND m.year = w.year
WHERE m.source_type = 'annual' GROUP BY m.state, m.year, gs.state_name, gs.state_fips

partitionedTables.name: fda_ndc_products
partitionedTables.comment:
FDA National Drug Code directory. Primary drug reference table; join hub for fda_drug_approvals (application_number), rxnorm_drugs (rxcui), and medicaid_drug_utilization (ndc = product_ndc). Covers all finished and unfinished drug products listed with FDA.
labeler_name is unstructured (no per-labeler id — product_ndc is per-product, and many products share one labeler). ref.canonical_org_entity carries it as an already-resolved identity (fda_labeler_name, with an LEI when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.

columns.name: product_ndc9
columns.comment: Normalized 9-digit product NDC (labeler[5]+product[4], zero-padded) derived from product_ndc. Join key to medicaid_drug_utilization.product_ndc9 — the raw hyphenated product_ndc and Medicaid's 11-digit package NDC never match directly.

columns.name: generic_name_normalized
columns.comment: Join key to fda_drug_shortages.generic_name_normalized. This table's raw generic_name never includes dosage form, and joins combinations with "and" in source order; fda_drug_shortages embeds the dosage form and joins combinations with ";" in alphabetized order, so a raw or case-insensitive join matches only ~4% of shortage drugs. Both sides derive this column the same way (GenericNameNormalizer): uppercase, strip trailing dosage-form phrase, split combination components, strip each component's salt suffix, sort, rejoin.

columns.name: product_type
columns.comment: HUMAN OTC DRUG or HUMAN PRESCRIPTION DRUG

columns.name: marketing_category
columns.comment: NDA, ANDA, OTC MONOGRAPH DRUG, etc.

columns.name: marketing_end_date
columns.comment: YYYYMMDD; NULL means still actively marketed under this listing, not "unknown" (D-253). A distinct-labeler count meant to measure current market concentration should filter to marketing_end_date IS NULL — otherwise every repackager/relabeler and discontinued listing that ever existed for a generic drug counts as a current manufacturer, which is exactly backwards from the concentration the count is meant to show.

columns.name: listing_expiration_date
columns.comment: YYYYMMDD the labeler's annual NDC listing certification lapses; distinct from marketing_end_date (a discontinuation the labeler actively reported) — a lapsed listing with no marketing_end_date means the labeler simply stopped re-certifying, not that the product was discontinued.

columns.name: rxcui
columns.comment: RxNorm concept ID — FK to rxnorm_drugs.rxcui (Phase 3)

columns.name: finished
columns.comment: True if finished drug product (vs. bulk ingredient)

partitionedTables.name: fda_drug_approvals
partitionedTables.comment: FDA drug approval applications (NDA, BLA, ANDA). One row per application. FK target for fda_ndc_products.application_number. sponsor_name is unstructured (no per-row id); ref.canonical_org_entity carries it as an already-resolved identity (fda_sponsor_name, with an LEI/SEC CIK when matched) — join there on the name rather than fuzzy-matching sponsor_name against sec company facts or ref.gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.

columns.name: brand_name
columns.comment: Brand or trade name of the drug product

columns.name: generic_name
columns.comment: Generic name(s) of the drug product

columns.name: product_type
columns.comment: Type of drug product (e.g. human prescription drug, human OTC drug)

columns.name: dosage_form
columns.comment: Dosage form of the drug (e.g. TABLET, SOLUTION FOR INJECTION)

columns.name: route
columns.comment: Route of administration of the drug product

columns.name: latest_submission_date
columns.comment: YYYYMMDD of the most recent submission action — a supplement (label change, manufacturing change, etc.), not the approval, for any application with post-approval activity. Use original_approval_date for the application's actual approval year.

columns.name: original_approval_date
columns.comment: YYYYMMDD the application's ORIG submission reached status AP (approved) — the application's real approval date and the only usable year dimension for an approval cohort (D-251). NULL when the ORIG submission's own status isn't AP in this feed (e.g. tentative approval only) or wasn't found. openFDA's drugsfda endpoint carries no separate filing/received date anywhere in the record (confirmed live against NDA020702/Lipitor's own ORIG entry), so review time (submission-to-approval duration) is not computable from this source — only the approval date itself. See fda_drug_submissions for the full per-submission history this is derived from.

partitionedTables.name: fda_drug_submissions
partitionedTables.comment: Full submission history per FDA drug application — one row per (application_number, submission_number). ORIG (submission_number 1, almost always) is the original application; SUPPL rows are post-approval supplements (label changes, manufacturing changes, new indications, etc.). An application's real approval date is its ORIG row's submission_status_date where submission_status = AP (also surfaced directly as fda_drug_approvals.original_approval_date). openFDA exposes no separate filing/received date anywhere in this record — only this status date — so review time (submission-to-approval duration) cannot be computed from this table or any other openFDA source; it is available only from FDA's own PDUFA performance reports. FK to fda_drug_approvals.application_number.

columns.name: submission_number
columns.comment: PK part 2 — ORIG is almost always "1"; SUPPL numbers increment per supplement

columns.name: submission_class_code
columns.comment: e.g. TYPE 1 (New Molecular Entity), EFFICACY, LABELING, MANUF (CMC)

partitionedTables.name: fda_drug_recalls
partitionedTables.comment:
FDA drug enforcement (recall) actions, one row per recall_number with severity classification (Class I/II/III), status (Terminated/Ongoing/Pending), and voluntary vs. FDA-mandated origin. Joins to fda_ndc_products only via recalling_firm/labeler_name text match — no structural NDC column is present in this table.
recalling_firm is unstructured (no per-row id). ref.canonical_org_entity carries it as an already-resolved identity (fda_drug_recalling_firm, with an LEI when matched, independently resolved from fda_ndc_products.labeler_name's own fda_labeler_name entry) — join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.

columns.name: event_id
columns.comment: Numeric ID FDA assigns to a specific recall event for tracking

columns.name: classification
columns.comment: Class I (most severe), Class II, Class III

columns.name: voluntary_mandated

AHRF ships raw physician/population COUNTS only — no per-100k rate column exists upstream — so primary_care_physicians_per_100k and total_active_physicians_per_100k are computed here from the matched count and population columns. primary_care_physicians is HRSA's "Phys, Primary Care, Patient Care" measure: non-federal MD+DO physicians in patient care, excluding hospital residents and physicians aged 75+, sourced from the AMA Physician Masterfile. total_active_physicians is all non-federal active MDs plus DOs (all specialties, not primary-care-filtered). AHRF is a wide file — each variable is a family of year-suffixed columns (e.g. phys_nf_prim_care_pc_exc_rsdt_23, phys_nf_prim_care_pc_exc_rsdt_22, ...) rather than one row per year, and each annual release adds a newest-year column while keeping older ones. AhrfPhysicianSupplyTransformer scans the header at load time for the highest-numbered suffix present and records which data year it picked in physician_data_year / population_data_year — so a stale suffix never silently ships; the years advance automatically as HRSA adds columns in future releases. rural_urban_code is the USDA ERS Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9; lower = more urban), useful for physician-shortage/rural-access analysis alongside the supply counts. partitionedTables.comment: CDC/NCHS mortality statistics at the state level (annual data also includes a United States total row). Unions annual (bi63-dtpu: NCHS leading/113-cause deaths and age-adjusted rate per 100,000, 2000 US standard population, 1999-2017) and weekly provisional data (source_type=weekly) from two Socrata vintages of the same "AH Weekly Death Counts by State and Select Causes" series: 3yf8-kanr (no COVID columns; loaded here from 2014 through 2019, not just 2018-2019 as its nickname might suggest) and muzy-jte6 (2020-2023, adds COVID-19 columns). Weekly rows surface the all-cause weekly total for the 3yf8-kanr years and the COVID-19 underlying-cause count for 2020-2023; source_type distinguishes annual from weekly, and age_adjusted_rate is populated for annual rows only.

columns.comment: Data year of deaths; MMWR year for weekly rows

columns.name: week_ending_date
columns.comment: Week-ending date; weekly rows only, null for annual

columns.name: state
columns.comment: State/jurisdiction; annual includes a United States total row

columns.name: cause_name
columns.comment: Cause-of-death name; NCHS leading cause (annual) or COVID-19 (weekly)

columns.name: full_cause_name
columns.comment: Detailed cause name (NCHS 113-cause for annual; COVID-19 detail for weekly)

columns.name: deaths
columns.comment: Number of deaths for the cause/period (COVID-19 deaths for weekly rows). NULL means CDC suppressed this week's count under its small-cell privacy threshold (typically <10), NOT that zero deaths occurred — confirmed live (2,296 weekly state-level COVID-19 rows carry this NULL). Do not treat NULL as 0 in a SUM; a plain SUM(deaths) already excludes these rows correctly by SQL's own NULL-skipping behavior, but an explicit COALESCE(deaths, 0) or an outer join that backfills a missing week with 0 would silently convert real suppression into a false zero. CDC signals weekly COVID-19 suppression two different ways in the source: some weeks omit the count field entirely, others include it as a "0" placeholder alongside a companion suppression flag field — CdcMortalityResponseTransformer checks that flag and nulls the placeholder case too, so every suppressed weekly COVID-19 row reaches this table as NULL either way.

columns.comment: Age-adjusted deaths per 100,000 (2000 US std pop); annual only

partitionedTables.comment: Provisional 12-month-ending drug overdose death counts by county of residence, from CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) program. Currently updated (not a frozen historical archive). County-level drug overdose mortality is NOT obtainable from CDC WONDER — its API rejects location grouping for National Vital Statistics System mortality data even though the interactive web UI offers it (confirmed live) — so this Socrata feed is the only public source for this grain. Counts of 1-9 are suppressed for privacy (see footnote).

partitionedTables.name: cdc_county_injury_mortality
partitionedTables.comment: County-level death counts and rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide, and firearm injury, from CDC's Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence (MIOV) tool. Both yearly and trailing-twelve-month periods. Currently updated. Complements cdc_county_overdose_deaths with suicide/homicide/firearm categories. Counts of 1-9 are suppressed for privacy (see count_sup); when suppressed, rate is NULL (the source has no crude estimate) and rate_m flags that a Bayesian small-area model was used instead, with its credible interval in rate_m_ci.

columns.comment: Death category: All_Homicide, All_Suicide, Drug_OD, FA_Deaths (all firearm deaths), FA_Homicide, FA_Suicide

columns.name: count_sup
columns.comment: Death count; suppressed (blank/flagged) when 1-9 deaths in the area for privacy

columns.name: rate
columns.comment: Crude death rate per 100,000 population; NULL when suppressed (see rate_m) rather than the source's -999 sentinel
columns.expression: CASE WHEN TRY_CAST(src."rate" AS DOUBLE) <= -900 THEN NULL ELSE TRY_CAST(src."rate" AS DOUBLE) END

columns.name: rate_m
columns.comment: True when the crude rate was suppressed and CDC substituted a Bayesian small-area model estimate (source field is a 0/1 flag, not a rate, despite its name)
columns.expression: CASE WHEN TRY_CAST(src."rate_m" AS DOUBLE) = 1 THEN TRUE WHEN TRY_CAST(src."rate_m" AS DOUBLE) = 0 THEN FALSE ELSE NULL END

columns.name: rate_m_ci
columns.comment: Credible interval for the model-based estimate when rate_m is true; NULL otherwise (source's -999 sentinel is mapped to NULL)

partitionedTables.name: va_medical_facilities
partitionedTables.comment:
Veterans Health Administration (VHA) medical-facility roster with geocoding — station number, facility type, name, address, city, state, ZIP, and (lat, lon). Static-snapshot table: the whole layer is re-paginated and the partition overwritten each run; history lives in Iceberg snapshots. Enables drive-time / distance-to-nearest VA-medical-facility computation for a veteran-population question (e.g. joined to census.acs_veterans by state or county). Cross-checked live 2026-09-13 against the real Palo Alto VA Medical Center (STA_NO='640'): city=Palo Alto CA 94304, LAT/LON = (37.40132, -122.13911), matches the real 3801 Miranda Ave campus location.
Facility-type coverage (facility_type, 1696 rows total, confirmed live 2026-09-13): PCCBOC 414, OOS 400, VTCR 318, MSCBOC 289, VAMC 171, MVCTR 73, DRRTP 15, HCC 12, CLC 2, MCS 2 — these 10 codes are the complete set present in the layer. VTCR (Vet Center) and MVCTR (Mobile Vet Center) together are 391 rows (23% of the table) — Vet Centers ARE included here, correcting this table's earlier sourcing research, which had assumed (without checking the live facility_type distribution) that this HIFLD layer was VHA-medical-only. None of the 10 codes correspond to a National Cemetery Administration or Veterans Benefits Administration facility, so this layer does not carry cemeteries or benefits regional offices; VA's own Facilities API (developer.va.gov, self-service API key required) would be needed to add them.
Source: the HIFLD-hosted mirror of VA's VAST (VHA Site Tracking) database at services2.arcgis.com/VFLAJVozK0rtzQmT — an individually-hosted ArcGIS mirror re-verifying VA's public-domain federal data (same accepted mirror pattern as housing.opportunity_zones). Re-verify-if-404s risk: if the HIFLD mirror stops serving this layer, the fallback is VA's own developer.va.gov Facilities API, which needs an instant-issuance self-service key and would broaden coverage to Vet Centers, cemeteries, and benefits offices in return.
street_address (from ArcGIS S_ADD1) is populated almost exclusively for Vet Center/Mobile Vet Center rows (VTCR 307/318, MVCTR 73/73 — confirmed live) — every other facility_type, including VAMC itself (1/171), mostly carries city/state/ZIP without a street. Use (city, state, zip) as the mailing/routing granularity when street_address is missing; (lat, lon) remain populated for every row and are the reliable input for distance computation.

columns.name: station_number
columns.comment: VA station number (STA_NO) — unique facility ID within the VHA system (PK)

columns.name: parent_station_number
columns.comment: Station number of the parent facility (PAR_STA_NO), when this row is a satellite/sub-facility

columns.name: facility_type
columns.comment: Short code identifying the facility category — VAMC (medical center), HCC (Health Care Center), MSCBOC/PCCBOC (Community-Based Outpatient Clinic variants), CLC (Community Living Center), DRRTP (Domiciliary Residential Rehabilitation), OOS (Other Outpatient Service), VTCR (Vet Center), MVCTR (Mobile Vet Center), MCS (a small, otherwise-unconfirmed clinic code — 2 rows). VA's own facility-type taxonomy; see the table comment for the full observed distribution and what's NOT included.

columns.name: facility_name
columns.comment: Facility display name (STA_NAME), e.g. 'Palo Alto VA Medical Center'

partitionedTables.name: ssa_oasdi_county
partitionedTables.comment:
SSA "OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County" (Tables 4 & 5, December snapshot) — one row per county per state per year (plus one state-total row per state/year), wide across the 8 beneficiary-type breakdowns SSA publishes: retired workers, spouses/children of retired workers, widow(er)s-and-parents, children of deceased workers (survivors), and — the reason this table was sourced — **disabled_workers_count/amount**, the SSDI caseload/payment figures no other table in this warehouse carries (census.acs_disability is self-reported disability prevalence, a different measure entirely). Sourced for shock-vs-disability-rolls analysis (Autor-Dorn-Hanson style): actual program enrollment against a labor-market shock, rather than a self-reported-prevalence proxy.
Deliberately excludes the same tables' "Aged 65 or older, by sex" (Men/Women) columns — a different demographic cross-tab of the same totals, not part of the beneficiary-type breakdown this table carries.
**Coverage**: 50 states, no DC (SSA's per-state directory listing has no dc.xlsx — confirmed live 13 Sep 2026; DC's OASDI figures exist only in the national/state-level Table 2/3 files, out of scope for this county-grain table) and no territories (PR/VI are published but excluded — no matching geo.counties FK). county_fips is NULL for each state's own total row (SSA labels it "Total, <State>" with its own state FIPS in the ANSI-code column rather than a real county code) — kept, not dropped, matching this schema's kept-total-row convention elsewhere; filter WHERE county_fips IS NOT NULL for a clean county-only sum.
**Akamai UA gate**: www.ssa.gov 403s a blank UA and a plain "GovData/1.0" identifier alike (confirmed live) but passes "Wget/1.21.3" — the opposite of CDC WONDER/BLS's own UA gotchas (those block a self-identifying UA and require blank/curl-like instead). The gate applies to the FIRST request, not just a re-download — both the source: block's headers and SsaOasdiCountyTransformer's own re-download need this UA set explicitly.
minYear 2005 (raw, pre-dataLag) reaches back to the oldest XLSX-format county file, FY2004 (2003 and earlier are PDF-only scans, not worth backfilling).

partitionedTables.name: medicare_geographic_variation
partitionedTables.comment:
CMS "Medicare Geographic Variation - by National, State & County" Public Use File — one row per (year, geography, age group), 2014-2024. Sourced to close the Medicare fee-for-service spending-by-state gap #67 identified: USAspending's award-based federal-spending totals omit ~$1.0T (FY2023) in Medicare FFS payments entirely, since they never post as discrete awards.
**Curated subset, not the full PUF**: CMS's source file has ~250 columns — payment, standardized-payment, and utilization-rate detail broken out separately for inpatient, outpatient, ASC, SNF, IRF, LTCH, home health, hospice, ED, procedures, tests, imaging, DME, ambulance, and several Prevention Quality Indicator (PQI) admission-rate measures, each further split by raw vs. per-capita vs. per-user vs. pct-of-total. This table carries only the headline totals (total/inpatient/outpatient/DME/hospice payment and per-capita figures) plus beneficiary counts and Medicare Advantage participation — the columns the spending-by-state question needs. Extending to the full category breakdown is a straightforward follow-up (same source, same grain) if a future need requires inpatient-specific or PQI-specific detail.
**Standardized vs. raw payment**: total_medicare_stdz_payment removes each area's geographic price adjustment (wage index, GPCI, etc.), isolating utilization intensity from local price levels — the figure to compare *how much care* an area's beneficiaries use. total_medicare_payment is the actual dollar amount paid — the figure for a spending/fiscal question. Use stdz for utilization comparison, raw for spending totals.
**Suppression**: CMS suppresses small-cell values (denoted '*' in the source) for privacy — these parse to NULL here via TRY_CAST rather than a fabricated 0. Small counties and the '<65'/'>=65' age-group splits are the rows most often affected; 'All' age-group rows are rarely suppressed.
**Geography**: geo_level is 'National', 'State', or 'County'. geo_fips is the 2-digit state FIPS or 5-digit county FIPS (FK to geo.state_ref/geo.counties); NULL for National rows and for the 'ZZ' catch-all state code CMS uses for unknown/foreign/territory beneficiaries (fully suppressed in every year checked). age_level is 'All', '<65', or '>=65' — filter to 'All' for a single row per geography/year unless the age split itself is needed.
**URL drift caveat**: CMS's data.cms.gov file path encodes an upload date (sites/default/files/2026-04/...) that changes when CMS re-publishes the combined file with a new year appended. Re-verify the URL against the dataset's landing page (data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-geographic-comparisons/ medicare-geographic-variation-by-national-state-county) if this table stops updating.
